question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , -63, -123, -243, -483, -963, -1923
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. -33.

GIVEN

• ? , -63, -123, -243, -483, -963, -1923

SOLUTION

• Each term = (previous term × 2) + 3.

• Check: -63×2+3 = -123; -123×2+3 = -243; -243×2+3 = -483; -483×2+3 = -963; -963×2+3 = -1923. ✓

• To find the first term: term × 2 + 3 = -63 → term × 2 = -66 → term = -33.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Work backwards from the second term: (-63 − 3) ÷ 2 = -66 ÷ 2 = -33.

NOTE

• For 'reverse-solving' a series, undo the operation: if forward is ×2+3, backward is (−3) then ÷2.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

B, Z, U, ?, N, L, G, E, Z
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. S.

GIVEN

• B, Z, U, ?, N, L, G, E, Z (positions 1–9)

SOLUTION

• There are two alternating series, each decreasing by 7 (with wrap-around, A=1…Z=26).

• Odd places: B(2) → U(21) → N(14) → G(7) → Z(26): 2−7=-5→21, 21−7=14, 14−7=7, 7−7=0→26. ✓

• Even places: Z(26) → ? → L(12) → E(5): 26−7=19, 19−7=12, 12−7=5. So ? = 19 = S.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The missing term sits in the even chain Z, ?, L, E — just subtract 7 from Z(26): 26−7=19 = S.

NOTE

• In alternate-letter series, split into two chains first; wrap position 0 to 26 (Z).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

NG, LD, JZ, HU, ?, DH, BZ, ZQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. FO.

GIVEN

• NG, LD, JZ, HU, ?, DH, BZ, ZQ

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: N(14), L(12), J(10), H(8), ?, D(4), B(2), Z(26) → decrease by 2. Missing = 8−2 = 6 = F.

• 2nd letters: G(7), D(4), Z(26), U(21), ?, H(8), Z(26), Q(17) → differences −3, −4, −5, −6, −7, −8, −9 (wrap-around).

• From U(21): 21−6 = 15 = O. (Then 15−7=8=H ✓.)

• So the missing term = FO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter is simple −2 (H→F). Second letter follows increasing gaps; 21−6 lands on O → FO.

NOTE

• When one letter has a fixed step and the other an increasing step, solve them independently.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

MU : FF :: WN : PM :: OB : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. HY.

GIVEN

• MU : FF :: WN : PM :: OB : ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letter: subtract 7. M(13)−7=F(6); W(23)−7=P(16); O(15)−7=8 = H.

• 2nd letter: the two letters of each output pair sum to 27 with the input's 2nd letter. U(21)+F(6)=27; N(14)+M(13)=27; so B(2)+?=27 → ? = 25 = Y.

• So OB → HY.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 1st letter −7 (O→H); 2nd letter = 27 − position (B=2 → 25 = Y). Answer HY.

NOTE

• Two complementary letters that add to 27 are 'position mirror + 1' pairs — a common SSC coding trick.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(GJ, JM, NR)

(IF, LI, PN)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (BC, EF, IK).

GIVEN

• (GJ, JM, NR) and (IF, LI, PN)

SOLUTION

• Across the three clusters, 1st letters step +3 then +4; 2nd letters step +3 then +5.

• (GJ, JM, NR): 1st G→J→N = +3,+4; 2nd J→M→R = +3,+5. ✓

• (IF, LI, PN): 1st I→L→P = +3,+4; 2nd F→I→N = +3,+5. ✓

• Option 1 (BC, EF, IK): 1st B→E→I = +3,+4; 2nd C→F→K = +3,+5. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check only the jumps between clusters: +3,+4 on first letters and +3,+5 on second — only (BC, EF, IK) fits.

NOTE

• In 'choose the analogous set' items, test the pattern between clusters, not just within a cluster.

question: What will be the sum of number of Fridays, Sundays and Tuesdays in December 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• December 2020 (31 days).

SOLUTION

• 1 December 2020 was a Tuesday, so 31 = 4 weeks + 3 extra days fall on Tue, Wed, Thu (Dec 29, 30, 31).

• So Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday occur 5 times; every other weekday occurs 4 times.

• Fridays = 4, Sundays = 4, Tuesdays = 5. Sum = 4 + 4 + 5 = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 31-day month has 3 'extra' days starting from its 1st day. Only the first-day weekday and next two get five occurrences.

NOTE

• Anchor date: 25 Dec 2020 = Friday, so 1 Dec 2020 = Tuesday (25 − 24 days = −3 weekdays).

question: What was the last day of the year 1919?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Wednesday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 31 December 1919.

SOLUTION

• Odd days count: 1600 years → 0; 300 years (1601–1900) → 1 odd day.

• Years 1901–1919 = 19 years = 15 ordinary + 4 leap (1904,08,12,16) = 15 + 8 = 23 odd days → 23 mod 7 = 2.

• Total odd days = 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 → 3 = Wednesday.

• So 31 Dec 1919 = Wednesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd days: 1900 yrs → 1, plus (15 + 2×4) = 23 → 2 for 1901–19. Total 3 = Wednesday.

NOTE

• Day map from odd days: 0=Sun, 1=Mon, 2=Tue, 3=Wed, 4=Thu, 5=Fri, 6=Sat.

question: 6 boys F, G, H, I, J and L are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). I is the third to the left of F. J and H are the immediate neighbours of I. L is to the immediate right of J. Who is third to the right of L?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. H.

GIVEN

• 6 boys around a circle facing centre; I is 3rd to left of F; J, H are immediate neighbours of I; L is immediate right of J.

SOLUTION

• Facing centre: left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise. '3rd to left of F' in a 6-seat circle = directly opposite F, so I is opposite F.

• J and H are on either side of I. L is immediate right (anticlockwise) of J, so J = H's opposite side; taking J adjacent to I and L next to J places (clockwise): F, L, J, I, H, G.

• Third to the right (anticlockwise) of L: L → F → G → H = H.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• In 6 seats, 'third to the left/right' always means the person exactly opposite; opposite of L in the ring F,L,J,I,H,G is H.

NOTE

• Facing centre → clockwise is left, anticlockwise is right; reverse it when they face outward.

question: 7 boys A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only four boys are to the right of C. A is second to the left of C. E is fifth to the right of D. B is second to the left of G. Who is sitting at the right end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. E.

GIVEN

• 7 boys in a row facing north; 4 boys right of C; A 2nd left of C; E 5th right of D; B 2nd left of G.

SOLUTION

• Facing north: left = lower position, right = higher position (positions 1–7 from left).

• 4 boys right of C → C at position 3. A is 2nd left of C → A at position 1.

• E is 5th right of D → D at 2, E at 7 (D at 1 is taken).

• B is 2nd left of G with B,F,G in seats 4,5,6 → G at 6, B at 4, F at 5.

• Order: A, D, C, B, F, G, E. Right end = E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Only 4 to the right of C' fixes C at seat 3 instantly; then E = D+5 forces E to seat 7 (right end).

NOTE

• 'Only N people to one side' is the strongest clue — fix that person's seat first.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AD89 : EB109 :: TK95 : LU115 :: HR88 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. SI108.

GIVEN

• AD89 : EB109 :: TK95 : LU115 :: HR88 : ?

SOLUTION

• Letters: swap the two letters and add 1 to each. AD → (D+1)(A+1) = EB ✓; TK → (K+1)(T+1) = LU ✓.

• HR → (R+1)(H+1) = S(19) I(9) = SI.

• Number: +20 each time. 89+20=109; 95+20=115; 88+20 = 108.

• So HR88 → SI108.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the letters, +1 each; add 20 to the number. HR88 → SI108.

NOTE

• Watch for 'swap + shift' letter rules; keep the number operation on the whole number as instructed.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LL17 : RT288 :: ? : KT360 :: AE21 : GM440
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. EL19.

GIVEN

• LL17 : RT288 :: ? : KT360 :: AE21 : GM440

SOLUTION

• Rule (X → partner): 1st letter +6, 2nd letter +8; number n → n²−1.

• Check: LL17 → (L+6)(L+8) = RT, 17²−1 = 288 ✓; AE21 → (A+6)(E+8) = GM, 21²−1 = 440 ✓.

• Partner is KT360, so answer X: 1st letter = K−6 = E; 2nd letter = T−8 = L; and n²−1 = 360 → n² = 361 → n = 19.

• So X = EL19.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the rule from KT360: K−6=E, T−8=L, √(360+1)=19 → EL19.

NOTE

• 288 = 17²−1 and 440 = 21²−1 signal an n²−1 pattern — recognise 'one less than a perfect square'.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to the fourth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

2369 : 2408 :: 1744 : 1783 :: ? : 3442
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3403.

GIVEN

• 2369 : 2408 :: 1744 : 1783 :: ? : 3442

SOLUTION

• Rule: first number + 39 = second number. Check: 2369 + 39 = 2408 ✓; 1744 + 39 = 1783 ✓.

• For the last pair, ? + 39 = 3442 → ? = 3442 − 39 = 3403.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant difference 39; subtract it from 3442: 3442 − 39 = 3403.

NOTE

• Confirm the operation on two given pairs before applying it to the unknown.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to the fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

754 : 3012 :: 68 : ? :: 51 : 200
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 268.

GIVEN

• 754 : 3012 :: 68 : ? :: 51 : 200

SOLUTION

• Rule: result = 4 × (number − 1). Check: 4×(754−1) = 3012 ✓; 4×(51−1) = 200 ✓.

• For 68: 4 × (68 − 1) = 4 × 67 = 268.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Multiply by 4 and subtract 4: 68×4 − 4 = 272 − 4 = 268.

NOTE

• 3012 = 4×753 and 200 = 4×50 reveal the 'times 4 of (n−1)' relation quickly.

question: In a certain code language, 'independence brings happiness' is coded as 'st pq lm' and 'independence comes after sacrifice' is coded as 'pq sm pz qs'. How will 'independence' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pq.

GIVEN

• 'independence brings happiness' = 'st pq lm'

• 'independence comes after sacrifice' = 'pq sm pz qs'

SOLUTION

• The only common word in both sentences is 'independence'.

• The only common code in both is 'pq'.

• So 'independence' = pq.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the common word to the common code — one shared word, one shared code.

NOTE

• Substitution-coding: intersect the two code sets to isolate the shared word's code.

question: In a certain code language, 'astronomy uses math' is coded as 'pn qr ta', 'math is subject' is coded as 'rs qr lm', and 'subject has chapters' is coded as 'lm po zr'. How will 'math subject' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. qr lm.

GIVEN

• 'astronomy uses math' = 'pn qr ta'

• 'math is subject' = 'rs qr lm'

• 'subject has chapters' = 'lm po zr'

SOLUTION

• 'math' appears in sentences 1 and 2; their common code is 'qr' → math = qr.

• 'subject' appears in sentences 2 and 3; their common code is 'lm' → subject = lm.

• So 'math subject' = qr lm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Find each word via the pair of sentences it shares: math→qr, subject→lm.

NOTE

• Cross-compare overlapping sentences to decode individual words in substitution coding.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

HN234, GG306, FZ378, ES450, DL522, BD656
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. BD656.

GIVEN

• HN234, GG306, FZ378, ES450, DL522, BD656

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: H, G, F, E, D, ? → −1 each, so last should be C (not B).

• 2nd letters: N(14), G(7), Z(26), S(19), L(12), ? → −7 each, so last should be E (not D).

• Numbers: 234, 306, 378, 450, 522, ? → +72 each, so last should be 594 (not 656).

• The correct 6th term is CE594, so BD656 is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• The number gap is constant +72; 522+72 = 594 ≠ 656 — the last term breaks it, so BD656 is the odd one.

NOTE

• In letter-number series, verify all three streams (both letters and the number) independently.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

LPI15, KNF22.5, JLC33.75, IJZ50.625, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. HHW75.9375.

GIVEN

• LPI15, KNF22.5, JLC33.75, IJZ50.625, ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: L, K, J, I → −1 each → H.

• 2nd letters: P, N, L, J → −2 each → H.

• 3rd letters: I(9), F(6), C(3), Z(26) → −3 each (wrap) → 26−3 = 23 = W.

• Numbers: 15, 22.5, 33.75, 50.625 → ×1.5 each → 50.625 × 1.5 = 75.9375.

• So the term = HHW75.9375.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Letters step −1, −2, −3; number ×1.5. Apply once more: H, H, W and 50.625×1.5 = 75.9375.

NOTE

• Multiplying by 1.5 = add half; wrap letter position 0 down to Z=26.

question: In 12 hours, how many times minute and hour hands of a clock will be opposite to each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 11.

GIVEN

• Count of times the hands are opposite (180° apart) in 12 hours.

SOLUTION

• The hands of a clock are exactly opposite once in every hour, except that in a 12-hour span one occurrence is 'lost' (around the 6 o'clock region overlap pattern).

• Hence they are opposite 11 times in 12 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• In 12 hours: coincide 11 times, opposite 11 times, right angles 22 times. Answer = 11.

NOTE

• The relative speed of the minute hand over the hour hand gives 11 events of each type per 12 hours.

question: Sum of the ages of 5 children born at interval of 4 years is 45 years. What is the age of the eldest child?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 17 years.

GIVEN

• 5 children born 4 years apart; sum of ages = 45 years.

SOLUTION

• Let the youngest be x. Ages: x, x+4, x+8, x+12, x+16.

• Sum = 5x + 40 = 45 → 5x = 5 → x = 1.

• Eldest = x + 16 = 1 + 16 = 17 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Middle (3rd) child's age = 45 ÷ 5 = 9; eldest = middle + 2×4 = 9 + 8 = 17.

NOTE

• For odd-count evenly-spaced ages, the average equals the middle term.

question: Father's age 1 year ago from present was 5 times of the age of his son 7 years ago from present. Son's age after 3 years from present is 22 years. What is the sum of present ages of father and son?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 80 years.

GIVEN

• (Father 1 yr ago) = 5 × (Son 7 yrs ago); Son's age after 3 years = 22.

SOLUTION

• Son's present age = 22 − 3 = 19 years.

• Son 7 years ago = 19 − 7 = 12 years.

• Father 1 year ago = 5 × 12 = 60 → Father's present age = 61 years.

• Sum of present ages = 61 + 19 = 80 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix son now = 19; father now = 5×(19−7) + 1 = 61; total = 80.

NOTE

• Convert every clue to 'present age' first, then combine — avoids sign errors on past/future ages.
